abstract: <jats:p>Preharvest sprouting (PHS) significantly reduces grain yield and quality. Identification of genetic loci for PHS resistance will facilitate breeding sprouting-resistant wheat cultivars. In this study, we constructed a genetic map comprising 1,702 non-redundant markers in a recombinant inbred line (RIL) population derived from cross Yangxiaomai/Zhongyou9507 using the wheat 15K single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) assay. Four quantitative trait loci (QTL) for germination index (GI), a major indicator of PHS, were identified, explaining 4.6–18.5% of the phenotypic variances. Resistance alleles of <jats:italic>Qphs.caas-3AL, Qphs.caas-3DL</jats:italic>, and <jats:italic>Qphs.caas-7BL</jats:italic> were from Yangxiaomai, and Zhongyou9507 contributed a resistance allele in <jats:italic>Qphs.caas-4AL</jats:italic>. No epistatic effects were detected among the QTL, and combined resistance alleles significantly increased PHS resistance. Sequencing and linkage mapping showed that <jats:italic>Qphs.caas-3AL</jats:italic> and <jats:italic>Qphs.caas-3DL</jats:italic> corresponded to grain color genes <jats:italic>Tamyb10-A</jats:italic> and <jats:italic>Tamyb10-D</jats:italic>, respectively, whereas <jats:italic>Qphs.caas-4AL</jats:italic> and <jats:italic>Qphs.caas-7BL</jats:italic> were probably new QTL for PHS. We further developed cost-effective, high-throughput kompetitive allele-specific PCR (KASP) markers tightly linked to <jats:italic>Qphs.caas-4AL</jats:italic> and <jats:italic>Qphs.caas-7BL</jats:italic> and validated their association with GI in a test panel of cultivars. The resistance alleles at the <jats:italic>Qphs.caas-4AL</jats:italic> and <jats:italic>Qphs.caas-7BL</jats:italic> loci were present in 72.2 and 16.5% cultivars, respectively, suggesting that the former might be subjected to positive selection in wheat breeding. The findings provide not only genetic resources for PHS resistance but also breeding tools for marker-assisted selection.</jats:p>
